pages.title: True Devotion - OpenArabic
pages.description: Seekers must guard against negligence and embrace prayer, supplication, honesty, and humility—for spiritual success rests on complete reliance upon God.

pages.title: On Sincerity - OpenArabic
pages.description: Sincerity is forged through honest self-assessment, compassionate action, and moral discipline—habits that yield inner peace and spiritual growth.

pages.title: A Life of Reading and Writing - OpenArabic
pages.description: A medieval Islamic scholar recounts intense reading, disciplined time management, and prolific writing, arguing that written works preserve and extend scholarly benefit.

pages.title: Rules of Scholarly Debate - OpenArabic
pages.description: Scholars treated ʻilm al-jadal as a distinct discipline, and both Ibn Khaldun and Ibn Taymiyyah emphasized clear rules and limits for disputation.

pages.title: Wives of the Prophet - OpenArabic
pages.description: When the Prophet's ﷺ wives formed two factions over gifts directed to Aisha, he defended her and resolved the dispute with wisdom.

pages.title: When Recitation Breeds Pride - OpenArabic
pages.description: Obsessive focus on perfecting recitation can distract from the Quran's meaning, breeding pride where there should be humility and devotion.

pages.title: Ten Daily Supplications - OpenArabic
pages.description: Seeking refuge with God ten times daily protects against Satan, as He commands an angel to repel the accursed enemy on the believer's behalf.

pages.title: Revelation Over Philosophy - OpenArabic
pages.description: The author warns that philosophical logic is harmful and divorced from true divine wisdom, which is found solely in the guidance brought by the messengers.

pages.title: Witnesses to God's Word - OpenArabic
pages.description: God's oaths by the sky and earth signify His lordship and affirm the Quran as a decisive word that distinguishes truth from falsehood.

pages.title: Night Prayer and Nearness to God - OpenArabic
pages.description: A devotional call to recognize the pain of spiritual distance, embrace patient endurance through trials, and fulfill duties to attain the hereafter.

pages.title: Following Desires - OpenArabic
pages.description: The passage warns that turning from revealed truth for personal desire leads to spiritual blindness, while guidance comes through faith and following divine revelation.

pages.title: A Prophet Warns His People - OpenArabic
pages.description: The Prophet ﷺ declares that every prophet must guide and warn his people, foretells future trials, and commands believers to uphold faith, justice, and rightful leadership.

pages.title: Sermons, Wit, and Sorrow - OpenArabic
pages.description: A medieval scholar captivated audiences with eloquent sermons and disarming humor—even as he bore the heartbreak of a disobedient son.

pages.title: Signs of Resurrection - OpenArabic
pages.description: On Judgment Day, humanity stands powerless. Yet even now the sky's rain and earth's growth are signs affirming the Quran as decisive truth.

pages.title: Directing Desire Toward God - OpenArabic
pages.description: Innate human powers—anger, appetite, and love for God—find true fulfillment only when directed toward their divinely intended purposes, while all other pleasures remain fleeting and vain.

pages.title: The Hidden Idolatry - OpenArabic
pages.description: Showing off in worship is a form of lesser idolatry—such deeds belong to the people they were meant to impress and are disowned by God.

pages.title: The Bridge to Paradise - OpenArabic
pages.description: In this life, following God's Straight Path determines the ease of one's passage over the bridge to Paradise on the Day of Resurrection.

pages.title: False Prophets - OpenArabic
pages.description: God's complete lordship necessitates guidance for creation, and His perfect attributes prove He would not support a false prophet who spreads corruption.

pages.title: Facing God's Tests - OpenArabic
pages.description: Believers are tasked with duties to God, self, and others, embracing this divine trial with patience and seeking guidance for ultimate success and happiness.

pages.title: Restraining Anger - OpenArabic
pages.description: Anger clouds reason, causing regrettable words and deeds. Strength, as the Prophet ﷺ taught, is self-control in anger—restraining your tongue and hands.

pages.title: Justice in the Field - OpenArabic
pages.description: Two anecdotes highlight misinterpretation of scripture and a judicial settlement where a governor resolves a crop damage dispute by ordering compensation.

pages.title: The Path to God's Love - OpenArabic
pages.description: True spiritual love arises from longing and complete surrender to God, not mere instruction, and it is wondrous that God loves His servant.

pages.title: Praise and Petition in Prayer - OpenArabic
pages.description: Every word of Al‑Fātiḥah is shared between God and His servant—and Imams Malik and Ahmad determined which phrases in prayer are obligatory.

pages.title: Faith and Worship - OpenArabic
pages.description: Gabriel's encounter with the Prophet ﷺ defines Islam, faith, and spiritual excellence—revealing worship as humility, devotion, and exclusive obedience to God.

pages.title: Death and Decree - OpenArabic
pages.description: A poetic affirmation of God's absolute power and decree, highlighting His creative control and judgment while contrasting the certainty of death with the fleeting nature of worldly life.

pages.title: What Was Created First - OpenArabic
pages.description: A companion asks the Prophet ﷺ about the first sign of the Hour, the first food of Paradise, and how a child's resemblance is determined.

pages.title: Brotherhood in Islam - OpenArabic
pages.description: The Prophet ﷺ teaches that Muslims must abandon envy and enmity, treat one another as brothers, and hold every Muslim's life, property, and honor as sacred.

pages.title: The Reward of Giving - OpenArabic
pages.description: A short anecdote that illustrates how sincere charity is described as a reward in heaven, while literal worldly claims to such rewards reveal a misunderstanding of spiritual giving.

pages.title: The Pilgrim's Conduct - OpenArabic
pages.description: Senior scholars advise embracing asceticism, guarding one’s speech, and keeping company with the obedient, illustrated by a pilgrim’s repeated prayer at Muzdalifah and his modest reliance on God.

pages.title: Raised in the Prophet’s Household - OpenArabic
pages.description: Raised in the household of the Prophet's ﷺ wife, this scholar absorbed wisdom and piety, growing to speak with the words of the truthful.
